title: Keep the bytes of a failed unpack out of the log, and for the team

blocks.text: The scrubber in 17.6 keeps card numbers out of the log, and it throws away the one thing the support desk keeps asking for: the bytes of a reply the client couldn't read. The team wants those bytes kept, but not in the log, which is shipped to a platform many people can search. They go to an `EvidenceStore` that only the team can read, labelled with the event's realm and with the part they came from.

`EvidenceKeeper` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/EvidenceKeeper.java` takes the scrubber's place in the logger, after `ProtectedLogListener` and before the writers. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`: `log` and `entryFor`.

When you're done, no raw bytes reach the writers, the store holds the exact bytes of every failed unpack, so that a test can be built from them, and everything else in the event reaches the writers as it did before. About 15 lines in total.
The tests build `receive` events the way a channel builds them, with and without a header, with an image from `DebugFilter`, and run one through a logger with a writer after the keeper.

cases.says: after a failed unpack the event keeps the exception and the marker but no dump, and the store receives the data under the event's realm
an event with a message and ordinary text keeps the same entries, and nothing is stored
the store receives the bytes the channel read, not the text of their dump
a header dump is taken out of the log and stored as the header, as well as the data
an image DebugFilter added is raw bytes too and is withheld from the log
the message in the event is left unchanged, card number included, for the masking filter to handle
in a logger, the writer after the keeper still receives the event once its bytes are stored

origin.section: 17.6 Raw Bytes in the Log Are Text, So a Filter of Your Own Has to Withhold Them

concepts: A failed unpack and DebugFilter put raw bytes into the event as entries the masking filter can't see, and a listener of your own replaces those entries, leaves messages alone and returns the event.
